raw_response:
Answer: A
Reason: In patients with pulmonary artery hypertension, chronic elevation of pulmonary pressures leads to right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation (cardiomegaly) and weakens the vessel wall, predisposing it to the formation of a pulmonary artery pseudoaneurysm; thus, the cardiomegaly is secondary to the underlying PA hypertension that also contributed to the aneurysm.
